stages.summary: Your baby is adjusting to life outside the womb. Movement is guided by newborn reflexes and sensory exploration of parents' voices and touch.
motor: Strong grasp reflex (clasps fingers tightly)
Startles (Moro reflex) to loud sounds or sudden shifts
Turns head side-to-side when resting on tummy
Keeps arms and legs flexed close to the body in fists
cognitive: Sees best at 20–30 cm (8–12 in), the distance to your face while feeding
Drawn to high-contrast black-and-white shapes and faces
Recognizes mother's and father's voices heard in the womb
Sensitive to smells, especially breastmilk and mother's skin
social: Calms to gentle rocking, swaddling, and shushing sounds
Reflexive smiles during REM sleep
Communicates hunger, fatigue, and discomfort primarily by crying
rhythm: Sleeps 16–18 hours across 24h in short 1.5–3 hour bursts
Feeds every 2–3 hours (8–12 times per day)
Wake windows are very short: 30–45 minutes max
stages.tip: Skin-to-skin contact ('kangaroo care') stabilizes baby's body temperature, blood sugar, and heartbeat while promoting bonding.

stages.summary: Baby becomes noticeably more alert. Growth spurts typically occur at 3 and 6 weeks, accompanied by cluster feeding and longer awake periods.
motor: Lifts head briefly (45°) when placed on tummy
Neck muscles strengthen; less floppy when supported
Hands open more frequently from tight fists
Smooth, reciprocal kicking of legs when lying on back
cognitive: Tracks faces and moving objects briefly with eyes
Shows sustained interest in bright colors and bold patterns
Turns head purposefully toward familiar voices
Quiets down to a calm voice, humming or white noise
social: First intentional social smiles emerge (usually around 4–6 weeks)!
Begins making soft vowel gurgles ('ah', 'oh', 'eh')
Makes sustained, meaningful eye contact during calm alert states
rhythm: Total sleep: 15–17 hours daily; wake windows: 45–60 minutes
Fussy 'witching hours' often peak in the evening
Cluster feeding is very common during growth spurts
stages.tip: Start doing 2–3 short bursts of tummy time (2–3 minutes each) daily on a firm mat or chest-to-chest.

stages.summary: A delightful, highly social stage! Your baby responds to your voice with joyful coos, big grins, and active arm batting.
motor: Holds head steady at 45–90° during tummy time, bearing weight on forearms
Brings both hands to mouth and plays with fingers
Swats and bats at dangling toys with uncoordinated swipes
Pushes down against your lap when feet touch a flat surface
cognitive: Tracks toys and faces smoothly across 180° midline
Studies their own hands with wonder and fascination
Distinguishes between familiar family members and strangers
Reacts happily to smiling expressions and lively voices
social: Delights in vocal play: long vowel coos ('ooo', 'aaa', 'eee')
Engages in 'conversations' by waiting for you to reply before cooing again
Chuckles and smiles broadly in response to peek-a-boo and tickles
rhythm: Total sleep: 14–16 hours; wake windows: 60–90 minutes
The longest night stretch often grows to 3–5 hours
Daytime shifts toward 4–5 defined naps
stages.tip: Establish a consistent 15-minute bedtime routine: bath, gentle massage, diaper, feed, and lullaby in dim light.

stages.summary: Babies are increasingly mobile, curious, and playful. Sleep patterns mature into adult-like sleep cycles, often causing the famous 4-month regression.
motor: Rolls from tummy to back, and starts attempting back to tummy
Reaches out accurately and grasps toys with both hands
Pushes up on extended arms during tummy time ('mini push-ups')
Strong head control with zero head lag when pulled to sit
cognitive: Reaches for objects within visual reach and brings everything to mouth
Laughs out loud at silly sounds and surprises
Recognizes bottles or breasts when hungry
Watches hands and feet move in space (body mapping)
social: Loud belly laughs, squeals, and blowing raspberries
Responds to changes in tone of voice
Expresses clear joy when loved ones enter the room
rhythm: Total sleep: 14–15 hours; wake windows: 90–120 minutes
Typical nap schedule: 3–4 naps per day
The 4-month sleep regression often causes temporary frequent night wakings
stages.tip: If baby shows signs of rolling, transition out of swaddles into a safe sleep sack to keep arms free.

stages.summary: Major leaps in independence: sitting without support, exploring first tastes of solid foods, and early babbling with consonant sounds.
motor: Sits independently without hands supporting for several minutes
Rolls fluidly both directions (tummy to back, back to tummy)
Passes a toy smoothly from one hand to the other
Rakes small items with fingers toward palm; bears full weight on legs
cognitive: Searches for dropped toys (beginning of object permanence)
Explores textures by banging toys together and chewing on teething rings
Responds to own name by turning head promptly
Shows distinct preferences for favorite toys and foods
social: Babbles consonant-vowel strings: 'ba-ba', 'ma-ma', 'da-da'
Uses sound to express pleasure, impatience, and curiosity
Understands emotional tone and stops briefly when hearing 'no'
rhythm: Total sleep: 13–15 hours; wake windows: 2–2.5 hours
Transition from 3 naps down to 2 solid naps (morning and afternoon)
Night sleep can reach 8–10 hours with 0–1 night feeds
stages.tip: Introduce iron-rich single-ingredient foods when baby sits well with good head control and shows strong interest.

stages.summary: Curiosity takes off on all fours! Babies pull up to stand, develop the fine pincer grasp, and begin communicating with gestures and first words.
motor: Crawls on hands and knees, scoots, or army-crawls
Pulls up to stand on furniture and cruises along edges
Masters the neat pincer grasp (picks up tiny puffs with thumb and forefinger)
Stands alone momentarily; may take first wobbly steps!
cognitive: Fully understands object permanence (finds hidden items under blankets)
Copies actions: bangs spoons, stirs cups, waves goodbye
Explores spatial relationships: drops items into bowls and dumps them out
social: First meaningful words appear ('mama', 'dada', 'ball', 'milk')
Waves 'bye-bye', shakes head for 'no', and points with index finger
Separation anxiety and stranger awareness peak around 9–10 months
rhythm: Total sleep: 12–14 hours; wake windows: 2.5–3.5 hours
Solid 2-nap routine (morning nap ~1h, afternoon nap ~1.5h)
Most babies can sleep 10–11 hours overnight without nighttime feeds
stages.tip: Baby-proof early! Secure heavy furniture and TVs to walls, cover low electrical outlets, and gate stairways.

stages.summary: Transitioning into toddlerhood! Independent walking, finger food mastery, increasing vocabulary, and expressing opinions and independence.
motor: Walks independently and starts attempting a fast toddler run
Bends down to pick up a toy from the floor without falling over
Stacks 2–3 blocks and scribbles with thick crayons
Drinks from an open cup and attempts eating with a small spoon
cognitive: Points to objects in picture books when asked ('Where is the dog?')
Follows simple 1-step directions ('Give me the ball')
Imitates everyday chores: sweeps, wipes surfaces, talks on toy phone
social: Uses 5–20 recognizable words consistently
Shakes head firmly and says 'no!' with enthusiasm
Shows empathy: hugs a crying sibling or cuddles a stuffed animal
rhythm: Total sleep: 12–14 hours; wake windows: 4–5 hours
Drop from 2 naps down to 1 midday nap (usually around 14–16 months)
12-month and 15-month sleep regressions may cause temporary bedtime resistance
stages.tip: Offer whole milk or fortified calcium alternatives in cups rather than bottles to protect developing teeth.

stages.summary: Active, chatty, and full of personality! Toddlers explore big emotions, combine words into short phrases, and love pretend play.
motor: Runs smoothly, kicks balls forward, and climbs stairs holding rails
Builds towers of 4–6 blocks; turns door handles and unscrews lids
Begins undressing simple clothes and putting on slip-on shoes
cognitive: Engages in imaginative pretend play (feeding dolls, driving cars)
Sorts toys by color, shape, or size
Understands concepts like 'big vs little' and 'in vs out'
social: 2-word combinations ('more milk', 'big truck', 'mama come')
Vocabulary reaches 50+ words with rapid weekly expansion
Big emotions and tantrums as desire for autonomy meets limited communication
rhythm: Total sleep: 11–13 hours daily
1 solid midday nap of 1.5–2.5 hours
Consistent calm bedtime routine is key to avoid bedtime battles
stages.tip: Acknowledge big emotions with calm empathy: 'You're upset that playtime is over. It's okay to feel sad, but it's time for lunch.'
